text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: Cannot be responsibly quantified from the information provided.

An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence that sex influenced the decision. Neither is another woman’s appointment.

Your stronger apparent academic credentials justify requesting clarification, but publication counts and PhD status may not capture all advertised criteria. Industry experience, teaching performance, and interview assessments could legitimately matter.

Follow up now on your unanswered request. Ask for the selection criteria, their weighting, feedback on your assessment, and how the appointee met essential requirements—especially whether a completed PhD was required. Check review or appeal deadlines immediately.

Raise sex discrimination if specific evidence emerges, such as sex-based remarks or inconsistent treatment—not simply because of the panel’s composition.
